The Petitioners have filed this petition against Respondents for the relief of compensation under Sec.166 of Motors Vehicles Act, 1989.

2. The brief facts of case is as under:
That on 09.01.2023 at about 7.20 p.m. Lakshmamma had been proceeding as a pillion rider on motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-40-EE-5142 being ridden by her son Manjunatha C. on Manchenahalli-Thondebavi Road, in between Belachikkanahalli and Hussainpura, Thondebavi Hobli, Gowribidanur Taluk, Chikkaballapura District,
at that time, one unregistered new Bajaj Pulsar motor cycle bearing came from behind at excessive speed in rash and negligent manner and dashed against the motor cycle on which Lakshmamma was proceeding, due to the said impact, she fell down and sustained grievous SCCH 5 injuries.

Immediately after the accident, she was taken to Chikkaballapura Government Hospital, after firstaid she was shifted to NIMHANS Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein she undergone surgery on 10.01.2023,
thereafter shifted to Prolife Hospital, Bengaluru for further treatment, wherein she died on 14.01.2023 during the course of treatment.
Further postmortem was conducted at Gowribidanur Government Hospital.

3. At the time of accident, deceased/Lakshmamma was aged about 54 years, working as coolie,

2 thereby earning Rs.25,000/- p.m.
petitioner No.1 and 2 are sons, petitioner No.3 and 4 are daughters of the deceased,

due to untimely death of the deceased, petitioners have lost earning member of the family, they have also lost love and affection, undergoing mental agony and also they havelost social, moral and economical support to a greater extent.

Out of the said SCCH 5 accident,
crime No.4/2023 is registered against the rider of the unregistered Bajaj Pulsar motor cycle before the Manchenahalli P.S. for the offences punishable under Sec.279, 337 & 304(A) of IPC.
Respondent No.1 is R.C.Owner and respondent No.2 is insurer of the said offending vehicle, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.
So that, prays to allow the petition and grant compensation of Rs.25,00,000/- with interest.
4. On service of notice, respondent No.1/owner has remained absent, hence placed exparte.
Respondent No.2/insurer has appeared through his advocate and filed written statement and denied entire averments of the petition.

Further stated that, petition is bad for non- joinder of parties and admitted issuance of insurance policy to Bajaj Pulsar bearing Reg.No.KA-50-EH-5720 and it was valid as on the date of alleged accident and if there is any liability to pay the compensation, it is SCCH 5 subject to terms and conditions of the policy.

The rider owner-cum-rider of the alleged offending vehicle namely Prakash A. was riding his vehicle without possessing valid and effective driving license and he also rode the said vehicle, without affixing the registration number.
There is no compliance of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of M.V.Act.
Claim made by the petitioner is higher, hence his petition is not maintainable.
Accordingly prays to dismiss the petition.

Gowribidanur, Chikkaballapura due to rash and SCCH 5 negligent riding of motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-40-EE-5142 dashed against the deceased motor cycle and caused accident, as mentioned in claim petition?
2. Whether the Petitioners are entitled for compensation? If so how much and from whom?
3. What order or award?

On the other hand,

In the said rulings their lordship have clearly held that, if any person i.e., driver has not holding valid driving license, then tribunals may award compensation on principle of pay and recovery etc., but admittedly the present accident was held on 09.01.2023.

So as per the Sec.150 of M.V.Act, the said section reads as follows;
SCCH 5 150. Duty of insurers to satisfy judgments and awards against persons insured in respect of third party risks.

- (1) If, after a certificate of insurance has been issued under sub-section (3) of section 147 in favour of the person by whom a policy has been effected, judgment or award in respect of any such liability as is required to be covered by a policy under clause (b) of sub-section (1) of section 147 (being a liability covered by the terms of the policy) or under the provisions of section 164 is obtained against any person insured by the policy, then, notwithstanding that the insurer may be entitled to avoid or cancel or may have avoided or cancelled the policy, the insurer shall, subject to the provisions of this section, pay to the person entitled to the benefit of the award any sum not exceeding the sum assured payable thereunder, as if that person were the decree holder, in respect of the liability, together with any amount payable in respect of costs and any sum payable in respect of interest on that sum by virtue of any enactment relating to interest on judgments.

SCCH 5 (2) No sum shall be payable by an insurer under sub-section (1) in respect of any judgment or award unless, before the commencement of the proceedings in which the judgment or award is given the insurer had notice through the court or, as the case may be, the Claims Tribunal of the bringing of the proceedings, or in respect of such judgment or award so long as its execution is stayed pending an appeal; and an insurer to whom notice of the bringing of any such proceedings is so given shall be entitled to be made a party thereto, and to defend the action on any of the following grounds, namely:-
(a) that there has been a breach of a specified condition of the policy, being one of the following conditions, namely:-
(i) a condition excluding the use of the vehicle - (A) for hire or reward, where the vehicle is on the date of the contract of insurance a vehicle not covered by a permit to ply for hire or reward; or (B) for organised racing and speed testing; or SCCH 5 (C) for a purpose not allowed by the permit under which the vehicle is used, where the vehicle is a transport vehicle; or (D) without side-car being attached where the vehicle is a two-wheeled vehicle; or Chandrashekara.

SCCH 5

So as per the language of the said section, the tribunals have no power to award any compensation, if any driver has violated the conditions of the policy nor who have not possessed valid driving license nor other conditions are violated as enumerated under Sec.150 of M.V.Act.

So inview of the said amendment to provisions of Sec.150 of M.V.Act and the said amendment came into force from 01.04.2022 and alleged accident was occurred after amendment, as such the rule of pay and recovery is not attracts to the present case.

Hence this tribunal comes to the conclusion that, it is just and necessary to issue directions against respondent No.1 to satisfy the petitioners by way of depositing the award amount within 60 days from the date of this order with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.

The Respondent No.1 shall deposit award amount with interest within 60 days from the date of this order.
The Petitioners are entitled for compensation at the ratio 25:25:25:25 in the award amount.
